subject: Data retention exception request — PII 0-retention / shortened logs
messages:
From: Amit Shah <amit.shah@finserve.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Cc: Maya Patel <maya.patel@finserveprocure.com>
Date: 2026-12-03T15:10:00-08:00
Subject: Thanks for the call — follow up on data retention

Neha — thanks for the demo earlier. Quick recap and one ask from our side related to compliance: FinServe is subject to stricter PII handling for customer financial identifiers. During the call we discussed options for minimizing risk on Redwood's side while still using hosted inference.

Our security team is asking whether we can get a contractual exception around retention of PII: specifically: 1) zero-retention for any fields flagged as PII (SSNs, bank acct numbers, full account numbers), 2) shortened logs for metadata (IP, user agent) to 7 days, and 3) clear controls around logging of prompt/response content (no persistent storage).

Can you confirm whether Redwood can support a 0-retention option for PII in hosted API, and what the operational limits are? If not, what alternative approaches (e.g., dedicated/private deployment, tokenization/redaction) would you recommend?

Maya (cc'd) is our procurement lead and will own the contract language. Happy to loop in security if you need more details.

Thanks,
Amit
Amit Shah
Head of Integrations, FinServe
amit.shah@finserve.com
+1 (415) 555-0198

From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Amit Shah <amit.shah@finserve.com>
Cc: Maya Patel <maya.patel@finserveprocure.com>, Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-12-03T16:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Thanks for the call — follow up on data retention

Amit — great to speak earlier, and thanks for the clear summary. Quick post-call recap and proposed next steps: 

Recap:
- FinServe asks: 0-retention for PII fields, 7-day retention for metadata, and no persistent storage of prompt/response content.
- Options: Hosted API with custom retention controls (limited), Redwood Dedicated (reserved capacity) or Private/VPC deployment for full control.

What I can confirm now:
- We can offer a zero-retention path for PII in dedicated/private deployments where you control the persistence layer. For hosted API, we have strict controls and can support redaction and minimal retention, but full 0-retention for indexed/observable artifacts requires dedicated/private or additional contractual controls.
- We support configurable log retention windows; typical hosted defaults are 30 days but we can propose a shortened schedule (e.g., 7 days) with an exception and SLA.

Next steps I propose:
1) Camila (SE/Security) to outline the technical approach for redaction/zero-retention and list any feature gaps.
2) I'll coordinate a draft retention schedule and contract language with Rafael for procurement.
3) If you can share your specific PII field list and any required audit evidence, we can align the controls and provide SOC2 artifacts.

I've attached a short SOC2 summary for context (SOC2_Audit_Summary.pdf). Will loop Rafael for the contract side.

Would next Tuesday 12/8 for a 30-min technical deep dive work for your security team?

Best,
Neha Kapoor
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
neha.kapoor@redwood.com

From: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>
To: Amit Shah <amit.shah@finserve.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Cc: Maya Patel <maya.patel@finserveprocure.com>
Date: 2026-12-04T09:30:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Thanks for the call — follow up on data retention

Amit / Neha — thanks for the notes. From a technical standpoint here are practical options and trade-offs: 

1) Hosted API (fastest)
   - Redaction at ingestion: we can implement field-level redaction in the request pipeline to strip or hash specified PII fields before they hit any runtime logs. This prevents PII from being present in persistent logs but does not change ephemeral in-memory processing.
   - Shortened retention: we can move request/response logs to a tier with a 7-day TTL for your account if we agree contractually and on scope.
   - Limitations: KV cache and some observability traces may retain minimal metadata for debugging; we can scope the telemetry collection for your account and reduce verbosity.

2) Dedicated / Private deployment
   - With Dedicated or Private, FinServe can control the storage tier and we can enforce true zero-retention for configured fields because logs can be turned off at the host level or routed to your managed storage with retention policies you control.

3) Application-side tokenization
   - As a mitigation, you can tokenize or encrypt PII before it reaches Redwood and perform de-tokenization downstream. This removes PII from the request payload entirely.

Actionable items for us to prepare for the call:
- A short list of PII field names and sample payload shapes (for redaction rules).
- Confirmation whether you need historical audit evidence (we can provide SOC2 artifacts and limited access logs for specific windows).

I'll prepare a 1-page technical brief comparing hosted vs dedicated for PII handling and attach to the call notes.

Regards,
Camila Reyes
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
camila.reyes@redwood.com

From: Amit Shah <amit.shah@finserve.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>
Cc: Maya Patel <maya.patel@finserveprocure.com>
Date: 2026-12-05T11:45:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Thanks for the call — follow up on data retention

Thanks Camila, that breakdown helps. Two clarifications from our side: 

- Primary ask: We need a contractual guarantee that any PII fields (we'll provide a definitive list) are never persisted beyond ephemeral memory for hosted API customers. If hosted can't provide that, we'll need to move to Dedicated or Private.
- Metadata: 7-day retention for IP/UA is acceptable but we need it written into the DPA/contract and visible in the logs export (so we can audit deletion).

Procurement next steps: Maya will own the contract redlines. Maya, can you share the preferred legal contact for Redwood? Rafael — looping you in for commercial & legal coordination.

Amit

On a related note, can you also confirm whether any generated embeddings could be used to reconstruct PII (we need assurance embeddings will not be stored or are reversible).

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>
To: Amit Shah <amit.shah@finserve.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Cc: Maya Patel <maya.patel@finserveprocure.com>, Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-12-06T10:00:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Thanks for the call — follow up on data retention

Amit / Maya — thanks for the clear asks. For contract and commercial next steps: 

1) Redwood is prepared to offer a contract amendment that specifies: 0-retention for identified PII fields in Dedicated/Private deployments; shortened 7-day retention for metadata in hosted with contractual SLA; and auditability via periodic export on request. We'll draft language for the DPA and a short SLA appendix.

2) Regarding embeddings: by default embeddings are persisted to support caching and retrieval features. If you require non-persistence we can offer a configuration to disable storing embeddings for your account or route them to your managed storage in Private deployments. We'll add explicit language covering reversibility and use of embeddings in the DPA.

Next steps:
- I'll have Legal draft the DPA appendix & retention schedule and share initial redlines (retention_schedule_proposal.xlsx and redlines_v1.pdf attached).
- Neha to coordinate a security deep-dive with your team on 2026-12-08 at 10:00 AM PT (tentative).
- Maya to confirm contract & legal contact for Redwood (I'll share our legal contact in the first redline).

If that works, I'll prepare the DocuSign envelope for signature after the redlines are resolved (link will follow).

Best,
Rafael Mendes
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
